There is a sound of gas leakage inside t.Fault Symptom: There is a sound of gas leakage inside the machine after connecting the gas source
Possible Cause 01: Poor connection of PU hose and air leakage.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 01: The fault disappears after the PU hoses in the machine is reconnected (see Figure 5-1).
Troubleshooting 01: Reconnect the PU hose with an insertion depth of about 20 mm.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 02: Pull out the PU hose (see Figure 5-1). The inserted part of the PU hose is obviously deformed and yellowed.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 03: Pull out the PU hose at the input end of the low-pressure regulator (see Figure 5-1). The bend is suffocated, and there is still leakage even when the gas source is connected.
Troubleshooting 03: Replace the high-pressure regulator assembly. See section 9.3.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 04: Disassemble the PU hose at the input end of the pneumatic module assembly.
Disassemble the PU hose at the input end of the low-pressure regulator and connect it to the inlet end of the gas source (see Figure 5-1).
After connecting the gas source, the leakage disappears.
Troubleshooting 04: Replace the low-pressure regulator assembly. See section 9.5.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 05: Other than leakage of the above-mentioned components.
Troubleshooting 05: Replace the pneumatic module assembly. See section 9.6.

Possible Cause 01: The gas source is not connected, or the gas source pressure is low.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 01: Check the on-site gas source pressure.
Check whether the gas cylinder's gas source pressure is lower than 1 MPa.
Troubleshooting 01: Connect a gas source with sufficient air pressure.
Possible Cause 02: The high-pressure sensor has a large zero drift or failure.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 02: If the self-inspection problem remains when the gas source pressure is greater than 1 MPa, the high-pressure sensor is faulty.
Troubleshooting 02: 1. Perform zero calibration of high pressure sensor (see section 6.2).
2. Replace the high-pressure regulator assembly (See section 9.3) if the problem remains.

Central gas supply or pressure relief va.Fault Symptom: Central gas supply or pressure relief valve is connected to the gas cylinder: Low gas source pressure Gas Supply.
Possible Cause 01: The gas source is not connected, or the gas source pressure is low.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 01: Check the on-site gas source pressure. Check whether the pressure of the central gas source is lower than 0.1 MPa.
Troubleshooting 01: Connect a gas source with sufficient air pressure.
Possible Cause 02: Central gas supply or gas cylinders supply gas after passing through the pressure relieve valve, but the gas source type is set to cylinder.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 02: 1. Press the Settings menu to enter the setting page. Change the gas source type to Central Air Supply. Restart the machine and the problem disappears.
Troubleshooting 02: Press the Settings menu to enter the setting page. Change the gas source type to Central Air Supply. Restart the machine.
Possible Cause 03: Low regulation pressure of the pressure relief valve.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 03: 1. Check whether the pressure of low-pressure gauge of the pressure relief valve is lower than 0.1 MPa.
2. Check whether the regulator knob of the pressure relief valve is loose.
It is the low regulation pressure of the pressure relief valve if either 1 or 2 is confirmed.
Troubleshooting 03: Tighten the knob of the pressure relief valve clockwise to increase the output pressure of the pressure relief valve.
Possible Cause 04: Dual-gauge pressure relief valve is stuck.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 04: 1. Check whether the pressure of low-pressure gauge of the pressure relief valve is lower than 0.1 MPa.
2. After loosening the pressure relief valve, re-tighten it. Repeat the operation 3~5 times. The problem disappears.
Troubleshooting 04: After loosening the pressure relief valve, re-tighten it. Repeat the operation 3~5 times.
Confirmation of Fault Cause 05: If it is confirmed that the pressure relief valve is not stuck (the fault remains after re-tightening the pressure relief valve), loosen the pressure relief valve adjusting knob, remove the connecting hose of the pressure relief valve, and then slowly tighten the pressure relief valve knob to observe Whether there is gas output at the output port of the pressure relief valve. If there is no gas output, the pressure relief valve is faulty.
Troubleshooting 05: Replace the dual-gauge pressure relief valve.
Possible Cause 06: The high-pressure sensor has a large zero drift or failure (V1.0).
Confirmation of Fault Cause 06: V1.0: If the fault disappears after upgrading the software (see 10) and zeroing of the high-pressure sensor (see section 6.2), the fault can be determined.
Troubleshooting 06: 2. Perform zero calibration of high pressure sensor (see section 6.2).
3. Replace the high-pressure regulator assembly (See section 9.3) if the problem remains.
Possible Cause 07: Short circuit or open circuit of the proportional valve (V1.0).
Confirmation of Fault Cause 07: Unplug the proportional valve cable (see Figure 5-2) and measure the proportional valve resistance. If the resistance is less than 9Ω, or >20Ω, the valve is faulty.
Possible Cause 08: Mechanical failure of the proportional valve (V1.0)
Confirmation of Fault Cause 08: If it is not a drive failure of the main board, connect the gas source. Set the proportional valve current to 90 in the diagnostic mode and open the inflation valve (see 5.7.3.3).
Touch the proportional valve after about 2 minutes. If the valve is heated with no flow at the gas injection port, the fault can be determined.
Troubleshooting 08: Replace the pneumatic module assembly (see section 9.6).
Possible Cause 09: The low-pressure sensor has a large zero drift or failure (V2.0 and above).
Confirmation of Fault Cause 09: When the gas source type is central gas supply, if the gas source pressure is greater than 0.1 MPa, but this self-check error remains, the low-pressure sensor is faulty.
Troubleshooting 09: Replace the pneumatic module assembly (see section 9.6).
